focus: Reading existing results instead of searching again, and answering from context instead of at all
description: Six questions in a row about an unchanged search. Tests the two opposite failure modes directly: re-running a search that nothing invalidated, and calling a tool for a fact already in the prompt.

turns.understanding: A complete one-way search on a date that resolves into next year.
subtasks: Search flights from Kolkata to Bangkok departing on Feb 10. Use the current year based on the travel context if needed. Show available options.

feedback.completedTask: Ran a one-way flight search for Kolkata → Bangkok on Feb 10 (resolved to 2027-02-10 from travel context) for 1 adult in economy and returned available options.
feedback.summary: Search completed for Kolkata to Bangkok departing 2027-02-10 (one-way). 3 options are available to display.
findings: Interpreted “Feb 10” as 2027-02-10 (next Feb 10 relative to the current travel context date).
Search: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, 1 adult, economy, outbound 2027-02-10.
Result set contains 3 available options (no filters applied).
limitations: Some option fields in the current environment may show inconsistent airport codes versus the requested city route; treat airports shown on cards as the authoritative display for this result set.
feedback.nextStep: Offer to narrow results by nonstop only, preferred airlines, or time-of-day.

turns.output:
✈️ I found 3 flights from Kolkata to Bangkok for Feb 10, 2027.

Note: Prices shown are per person.

turns.user: how long is the shortest one?
turns.understanding: A duration question about the options that already exist; nothing about the search has changed.
turns.why: Durations are per-contract. Re-running the search would discard a valid result set and rebuild the same one, which is the waste this script is built to expose.
subtasks: From the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10, tell me which option has the shortest duration and what that duration is.

feedback.completedTask: Checked the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10 and identified the shortest-duration option.
feedback.summary: Option 1 is the shortest-duration itinerary at 2h 10m total travel time.
findings: Trip context used: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, 2027-02-10 (3 visible options).
Shortest duration: Option 1, total duration 2h 10m (130 minutes).
limitations: The current option records show airport codes that don’t align with the Kolkata → Bangkok route (data inconsistency in the displayed contracts).
feedback.nextStep: If you want, I can compare the shortest-duration option (1) versus the cheapest option, or filter to nonstop/1-stop only.

turns.output: ✈️ The shortest one is option 1 at 2h 10m.

turns.understanding: The carriers present across the current options.
turns.why: The airlines in the results are contract data. The airline filter source options describe what could be filtered on, which is a different question from what the results actually contain.
subtasks: From the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10, list the airlines shown in the available options.

feedback.completedTask: Read the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10 and extracted the airlines shown across the available options.
feedback.summary: The currently visible options show 3 airlines: Air Canada, Air China, and Emirates.
findings: Airlines present in the visible options: Air Canada; Air China; Emirates.
feedback.nextStep: If they want, we can filter to a specific airline or compare options by stops/duration/price.

turns.output: ✈️ The airlines shown are Air Canada, Air China, and Emirates.

turns.user: what date did I give you?
turns.understanding: A restatement of the committed outbound date.
turns.why: The date is a stable search parameter in the prompt. Reading it back through a tool is a false positive.

turns.user: how many passengers is this for?
turns.understanding: A restatement of the passenger count, which has never been changed.
turns.why: Also an injected search parameter, and not volatile like a result count is.

turns.user: filter to the airline on the shortest one
turns.understanding: The shortest option was identified earlier, but its airline may never have been named aloud. Establish which carrier it is, then filter to it against the current search’s source options.
turns.why: The results are still valid and only the view narrows, so re-searching to "search that airline" is wrong — airline is not a search input. Reading the contracts first is allowed because the carrier is often not in the earlier duration answer, leaving nothing to resolve the reference against.
subtasks: In the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10, identify the airline for the shortest-duration option and apply a filter to that airline.

feedback.completedTask: Checked the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way results for 2027-02-10 to find the shortest-duration option’s airline, then applied an airline filter for that carrier.
feedback.summary: The shortest-duration option is operated by Air Canada, and results are now filtered to show only Air Canada options.
findings: Current trip context used: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, 2027-02-10, 1 adult, economy.
Shortest-duration option identified: Air Canada (2h 10m total duration).
Applied airline filter for Air Canada; result count changed from 3 options to 1 option visible.
limitations: The currently available results display airport codes that don’t match the Kolkata → Bangkok route context (e.g., LAX/BUR/ONT/SNA shown), so airport-code details may be unreliable in the visible cards.
feedback.nextStep: If you want more choices again, remove the airline filter or add a different constraint (e.g., nonstop/1-stop, departure time window).

turns.output: ✅ Filtered to Air Canada, the airline on the shortest flight.

turns.understanding: A confirmation of the outbound date, which the filter did not touch.
turns.why: A filter cannot move a date, so nothing needs checking. This catches a tool call made out of caution rather than need.
